content:
Rafael Mendes: We need to lock Comms Lead rotation for the status page transparency push. Also align on TTFU expectations so #eng-oncall isn’t guessing.

Talia Benson: +1. For rollout plan I need: (a) who’s on Comms Lead by week, (b) what “good” looks like (TTFU) + how we measure.

Sean Gallagher: Comms Lead should be explicit in the incident roles, not “IC does it if they remember.” Let’s keep it lightweight though.

Christine Wong: Proposal: Comms Lead is an add-on role for sev0/sev1 only. sev2+ can be IC unless Support asks.

Miles Thornton: Agree on add-on. In practice, if we wait until sev1 is declared, we still miss early comms. Can we say: if it looks like sev1+, Comms Lead gets pulled immediately?

Rafael Mendes: Yup. Trigger = “customer impact suspected” or “paging SRE” (not just formal sev).

Aisha Bello: From on-call perspective: if it’s a gateway-wide event, IC is already juggling mitigation. Having someone drive status updates helps a lot.

Allison Grant: Also gives us a single person to validate signals before we post. Reduces the ‘status says green but dashboards red’ situations.

Devon Price: On automation: incident-bot can assign Comms Lead at intake + nudge at T+10 if no public update. I can wire that behind a feature flag.

Rafael Mendes: Great. Let’s talk TTFU targets.

Sean Gallagher: We’ve been saying “10 minutes” informally. I’m ok committing internally to: Sev0/Sev1 first status page update within 10 min of incident declared (or first page), with an Investigating template. No need for details.

Christine Wong: Suggest we define it as: 10 min from “incident opened in bot” (more consistent than “first page”). That’s what we can measure.

Talia Benson: +1 for measurable. Can we do 10 min for Sev0/1, 20 min for Sev2? And “no update” is allowed if it’s clearly internal-only.

Rafael Mendes: Works. But we need a rule for “when to update.” Otherwise we’ll be gaming it.

Miles Thornton: Rule of thumb: if customer-facing symptoms (errors/latency) exceed thresholds for >5 min AND on-call is investigating, we post Investigating. If we’re still unsure on scope, we post “Some customers in <region> may be experiencing…” etc.

Jasmine Liu: From CS: what matters is we can point customers somewhere fast. Even an Investigating update with components/regions helps deflect tickets.

Sean Gallagher: We should coordinate with #eng-oncall: Comms Lead is NOT on-call’s job by default. It’s a separate rotation that can be pulled in.

Aisha Bello: Thank you. :pray: On-call can request Comms Lead, but shouldn’t be expected to write perfect copy mid-mitigation.

Rafael Mendes: Rotation idea: weekly Comms Lead “primary” + “backup.” Primary covers business hours, backup covers after-hours/weekend. If the incident happens off-hours and backup is asleep, IC posts first update using template, then Comms Lead takes over when awake.

Christine Wong: +1. Also: Comms Lead should join #incidents and #support when assigned.

Devon Price: I can have incident-bot auto-invite Comms Lead to the incident channel and drop the templates + checklist.

Allison Grant: Can we standardize what Comms Lead verifies before posting? Like: (1) which public component(s), (2) region(s), (3) current failure mode (errors vs latency vs streaming disconnects).

Miles Thornton: Minimal checklist (don’t block TTFU):
- pick best-fit component(s) (ok to be conservative)
- pick impacted region(s) (if unknown, say “multiple regions”)
- include workaround if we have one (fallback enabled, retries, etc.)
- avoid speculation / no RC until confirmed

Sean Gallagher: Exactly. First update is “we’re investigating.” Second update can refine scope.

Talia Benson: Who owns the rotation schedule? I can publish in Confluence + pin in #eng-sre.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll own initial schedule for next 6 weeks. Talia can keep it updated as we iterate.

Christine Wong: Volunteers for week 1/2? I can take next week as primary.

Allison Grant: I can be backup for that week.

Miles Thornton: I can do week after as primary.

Devon Price: Put me as backup week 2 (I’m around, and can dogfood the bot reminders).

Aisha Bello: Not volunteering for primary (on-call load), but happy to sanity-check the runbook wording before we hand it to on-call.

Jasmine Liu: For sev0/sev1 approval: please loop Support lead before posting “Resolved” if customer comms are ongoing. Otherwise we’ll have mismatched messaging.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s keep approval simple: Investigating/Identified/Mitigating doesn’t need approval (IC+Comms Lead). “Resolved” for sev0/sev1 gets a quick :eyes: from Support lead if available, but no blocking if they don’t respond in 5 min.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. We’ll write that into the roles doc.

incident-bot: Reminder (draft): TTFU target for Sev0/Sev1 is 10 minutes from incident open. Use `/statuspage draft investigating` to generate copy.

Devon Price: lol perfect timing. I’ll update the reminder text once we finalize.

Talia Benson: Action items I captured:
1) Rafael: post 6-week Comms Lead primary/backup schedule + where it lives
2) Devon: incident-bot assignment + T+10 reminder (feature flagged)
3) Christine/Miles: propose quick checklist + templates tweaks
4) Sean/Jasmine: confirm approval rule for sev0/1 resolved updates

Rafael Mendes: Sounds right. I’ll also ping #eng-oncall with “what to expect” so they don’t think we’re adding work.

Sean Gallagher: Please include: when Comms Lead is assigned, they own status updates + CS coordination; IC stays focused on mitigation.

Christine Wong: I’ll drop a short blurb we can paste to #eng-oncall.

Rafael Mendes: Thanks all. Let’s aim to start rotation Monday and treat it as a 2-week dogfood before we call it “policy.”
